テニスの混合ダブルスでは柴原瑛菜、フレンド原ジェイ組が青山修子、楠原悠介組をストレートで下して優勝。同大会のテニス競技の決勝が日本人対決となったのは今回が初めてだった。

サッカー男子決勝では日本が韓国に０─１で敗戦。バレーボール男子決勝で、日本はイランにセットカウント１─３で負けた。

日本は今大会、３日の競技を終えた時点で銀メダルは９５個で銅メダルは９１個。金メダルと合わせて２６９個と、３４１個の中国に次ぐ２位のメダル数を記録している。

item.title: PGA club pro Michael Block takes 1-stroke lead after 36 holes in Allentown
item.description: Michael Block needed only 30 shots on the back nine and posted a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Saturday to take a one-stroke lead after two rounds of the inaugural Jefferson Lehigh Valley Classic in Allentown, Pa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Block needed only 30 shots on the back nine and posted a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Saturday to take a one-stroke lead after two rounds of the inaugural Jefferson Lehigh Valley Classic in Allentown, Pa. Block, a 50-year-old PGA Tour Champions rookie, stands at 11 under through 36 holes. That puts him one ahead of New Zealand's Steven Alker and two ahead of first-round co-leader Richard Green of Australia. Block, who continues to serve as the head golf professional at Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club in Mission Viejo, Calif., gained a following with a tie for 15th place at the 2023 PGA Championship. Block, who shot a 4-under par 66 on Friday, opened with back-to-back birdies on Saturday. He parred the last seven holes on the front nine, then birdied five of the first seven holes coming in. He is highly appreciative of the welcome he has received on the tour. "So the support I have from the fellow Champions Tour players is amazing," Block said. "The relationships I've gotten in six events/seven, is crazy, and I really appreciate those guys. These guys have been living the Tour life, the PGA Tour life and Champions Tour life for, you know, 20-30 years, and I'm just out here -- and they know my scenario. I'm out here as a club pro, and being out here for my seventh event in my life, and they really support me, which is really cool. Trust me, it helps a lot." In Block's fifth Champions start at The Ally Challenge five weeks ago, he also held the lead after 36 holes. But he was passed by Alker during the final round and ended up tied for third. What did Block learn from that experience? "Yeah, from Ally, just keep being you," he said. "Like, don't try to be the quiet Michael. Quiet Michael doesn't work. Michael having fun works. Michael being quiet, Michael trying to be somebody he's not doesn't work. That's what I'm going to do tomorrow." In contrast to Block, who's happy just to be on the verge of qualifying for the Charles Schwab Cup playoffs, Alker has won three times in 2026, owns 13 PGA Tour Champions titles and ranks No. 3 on the Schwab Cup money list. The 55-year-old has posted matching 65s and, like Block, played bogey-free golf on Saturday. He shot 31 on the inward half and played the par-3's in 2-under. Alker is well aware the gallery will be flocking to Block on Sunday. "He's got a great following and I think the crowds will be good tomorrow and want him to do well," Alker said. "He's a bit different, he likes to talk about things. It's fun. I kind of like watching him play a little bit, see how he goes about the game. Not that I'll take a whole lot of it forward, but I just like watching him play and how he goes about his game. "He's got game, I've got to bring it tomorrow." Ryan Armour fired a 64 to move into fourth at 8-under. Tag Ridings (65), South Korea's Y.E. Yang (69) and Sweden's Robert Karlsson (69) share fifth at 7-under. Yang and Karlsson joined Green atop the leaderboard after the first round. --Field Level Media

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝地区シリーズ開幕、村上が先制2ラン ドジャース大谷1安打
item.description: ［クリーブランド ３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［クリーブランド　３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のプレーオフ、地区シリーズ（５回戦制）が３日、各地で開幕。ホワイトソックスの村上宗隆内野手はガーディアンズ戦に「４番・一塁」で出場し、四回にポストシーズン初本塁打となる先制２ランを放った。

ライトスタンドに約１３４メートルの一発をたたき込んだ村上は試合後、通訳を介し「準備はできていた。シーズンを通じてこの瞬間に向けて備えてきた」とコメントした。村上は４打数２安打２打点と活躍。ホワイトソックスは３─０でシリーズ初戦を制した。

ドジャースの大谷翔平選手はブレーブス戦に「２番・指名打者」で出場し、４打数１安打。ドジャースは５─３で勝った。先発のタリク・スクバル投手が６回１失点の好投で勝利投手となった。

item.title: México dice que investigación de la FDA sobre la lechuga no identificó la fuente de la contaminación
item.description: El Ministerio de Salud de México dijo el sábado que la investigación de la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de EEUU (FDA por su sigla en inglés ) sobre el brote del parásito Cyclospora, relacionado con la lechuga iceberg troceada de Taylor Farms en México, no identificó de forma concluyente el origen de la contaminación.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Ministerio de Salud de México dijo el sábado que la investigación de la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de EEUU (FDA por su sigla en inglés ) sobre el brote del parásito Cyclospora, relacionado con la lechuga iceberg troceada de Taylor Farms en México, no identificó de forma concluyente el origen de la contaminación. La Cofepris, el organismo regulador de la seguridad alimentaria de México, señaló que los análisis realizados por su laboratorio nacional de referencia en materias primas, productos terminados y agua de las instalaciones investigadas en relación con el brote dieron negativo para el parásito Cyclospora. El regulador añadió que los resultados ambientales por sí solos no constituyen una prueba concluyente de que los productos agrícolas fueran la fuente de la contaminación. La FDA [USN:L6N45O12Z TEXT:"declaró el viernes"] que había encontrado un fuerte vínculo epidemiológico y de trazabilidad entre el brote y la lechuga iceberg troceada retirada del mercado, producida por Taylor Farms en México, pero señaló que no había pruebas suficientes para determinar cómo se produjo la contaminación. La agencia informó de dos muestras ambientales positivas para Cyclospora en México: una procedente de las aguas residuales que salían de una planta de procesamiento y otra de una zanja de drenaje en una explotación de lechuga iceberg. Los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) declararon el fin del brote el 11 de septiembre. El brote afectó a 12.883 personas en 21 estados, provocó la hospitalización de 570 personas y se relacionó con dos fallecimientos. México afirmó que había cooperado durante toda la investigación, proporcionando información sobre la trazabilidad, inspecciones y muestras, y que continuaría la cooperación técnica con las autoridades sanitarias estadounidenses.

item.title: Mexico says FDA lettuce probe did not conclusively identify contamination source
item.description: Mexico's Health Ministry said on Saturday that a US Food and Drug Administration investigation into the cyclospora parasite outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico did not conclusively identify the source of contamination.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mexico's Health Ministry said on Saturday that a US Food and Drug Administration investigation into the cyclospora parasite outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico did not conclusively identify the source of contamination. Mexico's food-safety regulator Cofepris said tests conducted by its national reference laboratory on raw materials, finished products and water from the facility investigated in the outbreak were negative for the cyclospora parasite. The regulator added that environmental findings alone do not constitute conclusive evidence that agricultural products were the source of contamination. The FDA said [USN:L4N45O17K TEXT:"on Friday"] it found a strong epidemiological and traceback link between the outbreak and recalled shredded iceberg lettuce produced by Taylor Farms in Mexico, but said there was insufficient evidence to determine how contamination occurred. The agency reported two environmental samples positive for cyclospora in Mexico, one from wastewater leaving a processing facility and another from a drainage ditch at an iceberg lettuce farm. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention declared the outbreak over on September 11. The outbreak sickened 12,883 people in 21 states, hospitalized 570 and was linked to two deaths. Mexico said it cooperated throughout the investigation, providing traceability information, inspections and samples, and would continue technical cooperation with US health authorities.

item.title: -Lula e Flávio travam disputa acirrada e eleição deve ir para 2º turno, mostram pesquisas
item.description: Pesquisas divulgadas neste sábado mostraram uma disputa apertada na corrida presidencial entre os dois principais candidatos, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que tenta a reeleição, e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pesquisas divulgadas neste sábado mostraram uma disputa apertada na corrida presidencial entre os dois principais candidatos, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que tenta a reeleição, e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). A corrida deve ser decidida apenas no segundo turno, daqui a três semanas, de acordo com os levantamentos. Para um candidato ser eleito no primeiro turno, no domingo, ele precisa ter mais de 50% dos votos válidos, quando não são computados os votos brancos e nulos. Veja o desempenho de Lula e Flávio nos levantamentos divulgados neste sábado: DATAFOLHA Lula - 45% Flávio - 42% Margem de erro de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. QUAEST Lula - 46% Flávio - 45% Margem de erro de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. CNT/MDA Lula - 47,8% Flávio - 42,1% Margem de erro de 2,2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. (Redação São Paulo)

item.title: Lula tem 46% dos votos válidos contra 45% de Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno, mostra Quaest
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) estão em empate técnico nos votos válidos do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com vantagem numérica de 1 ponto percentual para o petista, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) estão em empate técnico nos votos válidos do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com vantagem numérica de 1 ponto percentual para o petista, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado. Lula tem 46% dos votos válidos, quando são excluídos os brancos, nulos e indecisos, enquanto Flávio soma 45%. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. Para vencer no primeiro turno no domingo, um candidato precisa ter mais de 50% dos votos válidos. Nos chamados votos totais, o presidente aparece com 40% (eram 39% na pesquisa anterior), contra 38% do senador de oposição (eram 34%). Os indecisos somam 3% (eram 5% na pesquisa anterior), enquanto aqueles que dizem que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum candidato chegam a 10%, mesma parcela da pesquisa anterior. Já num eventual segundo turno entre os dois, Flávio Bolsonaro aparece numericamente à frente, com 44% (eram 42%), enquanto Lula registra os mesmos 42% do último levantamento.

item.title: Top 25 roundup: No. 25 Mizzou runs it up in rout of No. 8 Florida
item.description: Austin Simmons threw for 340 yards and two touchdowns, Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards and three scores, and No. 25 Missouri's defense shut down star running back Jadan Baugh in a 45-17 victory Saturday afternoon over No. 8 Florida in Columbia, Mo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Austin Simmons threw for 340 yards and two touchdowns, Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards and three scores, and No. 25 Missouri's defense shut down star running back Jadan Baugh in a 45-17 victory Saturday afternoon over No. 8 Florida in Columbia, Mo. Roberts broke two long second-half runs, one for 77 yards and later an 80-yard touchdown for the Tigers, who scored 35 straight points after the score was tied 10-10 late in the first half, scoring on six straight possessions. Mizzou coach Eli Drinkwitz improved to 2-10 against teams ranked in the Top 10 of the Associated Press poll. Simmons hooked up with Donovan Olugbode on a 47-yard touchdown pass, and with Caleb Goodie Sr. on a 31-yard score in the second quarter. Cayden Lee led the Tigers (4-1, 1-1 Southeastern Conference), with 110 receiving yards on eight catches. Simmons finished 23-of-30 passing. Baugh, a Heisman Trophy candidate after the first month of the season, gained only 13 rushing yards on 12 carries for the Gators (4-1, 2-1). He came in with 11 touchdowns to lead FBS, and had rushed for at least 100 yards in five straight games dating back to last season. No. 2 Georgia 38, Vanderbilt 14 Gunner Stockton completed 25 of 32 passes for 295 yards and three touchdowns to help lead the Bulldogs to victory over the Commodores in Athens, Ga. Stockton connected with 10 receivers, including Dwight Phillips Jr., who had five catches for 75 yards and a score. The Bulldogs (5-0, 3-0 SEC) have won all their games by at least 24 points. They outscored the Commodores 17-0 in the second half after going into halftime with a 21-14 lead. Vanderbilt (3-2, 0-2) was without freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, who was scratched before the game with an undisclosed injury. In his place, Blaze Berlowitz completed 12 of 23 passes for 190 yards and a touchdown. Junior Sherrill posted seven receptions for 107 yards and a score for the Commodores, who dropped their second straight game. No. 3 Notre Dame 37, North Carolina 26 CJ Carr threw for four touchdowns and ran for another as the Fighting Irish beat the Tar Heels in rainy conditions in Chapel Hill, N.C. Jordan Faison caught two touchdown passes as part of an eight-catch, 132-yard receiving effort for Notre Dame (5-0). Carr completed 21 of 29 passes for 234 yards. Jonaz Walton rushed for 120 yards on 23 carries. Billy Edwards Jr. threw for three touchdowns, two interceptions and 208 yards for North Carolina (2-2), which was held to 285 yards of total offense. Jordan Shipp had 109 receiving yards on seven catches. No. 4 Miami 41, Clemson 13 Mark Fletcher Jr. ran for two touchdowns and Darian Mensah passed for a TD and ran for another to lead the Hurricanes in a rout of the host Tigers. Miami (5-0, 3-0 Atlantic Coast Conference) moved into sole possession of first place in the league standings while beating Clemson (3-2, 2-1) on its home field for the first time since 2010. Fletcher finished with 77 yards on 16 carries. Mensah completed 18 of 27 passes for 227 yards. The Hurricanes' defense recorded six sacks, including five in the first half, against Clemson quarterback Tait Reynolds. He completed 29 of 44 passes for 295 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, which resulted in a 39-yard pick-six by Miami's JJ Dunnigan to close the scoring. No. 5 Ohio State 31, No. 14 Iowa 14 Jeremiah Smith set two more school records and strengthened his Heisman Trophy candidacy as the Buckeyes defeated the Hawkeyes in Iowa City. Smith, a junior, made his 36th career touchdown catch in the third quarter to surpass Chris Olave's school record and give Ohio State a 24-6 lead. On Ohio State's next drive, Smith's 10th catch of the game was his 206th for the Buckeyes to move one ahead of former record-holder Emeka Egbuka. Smith finished with 11 catches for 206 yards. Iowa finished with just 238 total yards and lost the turnover battle 2-0. No. 6 Indiana 47, Rutgers 15 Josh Hoover was 20-for-27 passing for 251 yards and four touchdowns, Turbo Richard racked up a career-high 204 yards and a score on the ground and the Hoosiers thrashed the Scarlet Knights in Piscataway, N.J. The Hoosiers (5-0, 2-0 Big Ten) extended the nation's longest winning streak to 21. Lee Beebe Jr. had a big second half to finish with 122 rushing yards and a touchdown, while Charlie Becker made eight catches for 107 yards and two TDs. Indiana became the first Big Ten team with two 100-yard rushers and two 100-yard receivers in one game since 1995. Rutgers' AJ Surace relieved Dylan Lonergan at quarterback before halftime, with Lonergan apparently injured on a QB sneak attempt. Surace was the more effective passer for the Scarlet Knights (1-4, 0-2), with 128 yards and a 53-yard touchdown to Ben Black III. No. 7 Alabama 56, No. 16 Mississippi State 23 Keelon Russell totaled four touchdowns, as the Crimson Tide rolled past the Bulldogs in an SEC clash in Starkville, Miss. Russell threw for 285 yards and three touchdowns and ran for one more. Rico Scott had 56 receiving yards and two touchdowns for Alabama (5-0, 3-0 SEC), which is 5-0 for the first time in Kalen DeBoer's three seasons. Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor completed 19 of 34 passes for 258 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions. The Bulldogs have lost 17 straight games against the Crimson Tide. Taylor went to the locker room with an undisclosed injury early in the fourth quarter, and reserve Parker Puckett finished the game under center. No. 10 BYU 17, TCU 10 Quarterback Bear Bachmeier rushed for two touchdowns and Faletau Satuala recorded a key interception as the Cougars downed the Horned Frogs in Big 12 play at Fort Worth, Texas. Bachmeier rushed for 66 yards on 15 carries and completed 11 of 24 passes for 62 yards for BYU (4-0, 2-0 Big 12), which has started 4-0 in three consecutive seasons for the first time in program history. Star running back LJ Martin carried the ball just twice for 16 yards before exiting in the first quarter with a right leg injury. The reigning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year was ruled out at halftime. Jaden Craig was 18-of-25 passing for 187 yards, one touchdown and one interception for TCU (2-3, 0-2). Kari Ashley had six receptions for 108 yards and one touchdown and Jeremy Payne had 100 yards from scrimmage (77 rushing, 23 receiving). No. 11 LSU 63, McNeese 14 Sam Leavitt passed for three touchdowns in limited action, Corey Barber Jr. caught two of the scoring passes, Harlem Berry and Stacy Gage each rushed for more than 100 yards as the host Tigers thrashed the FCS-level Cowboys in Baton Rouge, La. Leavitt, who has been hampered by a hamstring injury, did not run the ball and played just the first half before being relieved by Landen Clark with LSU (4-1) leading 35-0. Leavitt passed for 176 yards and an interception. Barber, a freshman who had just one reception for 15 yards before Saturday, finished with seven catches for 83 yards and his first career TDs. Berry had the first 100-yard rushing game of his two-year career, finishing with 125 yards and a score, and Gage rushed for 110 yards and two TDs on six carries. The Tigers outgained McNeese (2-4) 731-196 and finished with a 37-6 advantage in first downs. No. 12 Texas Tech 29, Colorado 7 John Curry intercepted a pass in the end zone for a touchdown, Brice Pollock had two interceptions and Malik Esquerra added another pick as the Red Raiders rallied for a victory over the Buffaloes in Boulder, Colo. All three third-quarter Colorado (2-3, 0-2 Big 12) drives ended in interceptions as the Red Raiders (5-0, 2-0) overcame a 7-3 halftime deficit. As Curry rushed off the edge with 7:10 remaining in the game, he reached up and intercepted Colorado quarterback Isaac Wilson's pass in the end zone for a 22-7 lead. Texas Tech's Will Hammond threw for 134 yards and a touchdown. J'Koby Williams rushed for 88 yards and Quinten Joyner ran in a score. Wilson was 26 of 44 for 290 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Joseph Williams caught 10 passes for 93 yards and a score and threw an interception on a trick play. No. 17 Tennessee 24, Auburn 14 DeSean Bishop rushed for a career-high 220 yards and three second-half touchdowns to rally the Volunteers past the Tigers in the first matchup between these SEC foes since 2020 in Knoxville, Tenn. The former walk-on from Knoxville carried 34 times while becoming the first Tennessee running back to go for 200 yards and three scores since Eric Gray in 2019. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel benched freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon late in the first half after he went 3-for-8 passing for no yards and one interception. Backup George MacIntyre completed 8 of 10 passes for 86 yards. Auburn's Byrum Brown was 22-for-33 passing for 159 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He rushed for 107 yards on 19 attempts and scored the first touchdown for the Tigers, who built a 7-3 halftime lead. No. 18 Southern California 25, Washington 21 The Trojans scored a pair of third-quarter touchdowns less than two minutes apart, then held firm on the Huskies' final drive to survive with a win in Los Angeles. The Trojans (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten Conference) surrendered a pair of fourth-down conversions that allowed the Huskies (3-2, 0-2) to advance into the red zone with less than a minute remaining in regulation. USC's defense buckled down, however. USC's Jayden Maiava finished with one of his more statistically muted efforts, going 21-of-34 passing for 245 yards with a touchdown and an interception. King Miller led the Trojans with 81 yards rushing. Demond Williams Jr. finished 15-of-26 passing for 198 yards and one touchdown and Brian Bonner rushed for 89 yards for Washington. No. 20 Houston 27, UCF 17 Conner Weigman scored three times on the ground in the second half as the host Cougars shrugged off a ragged first 40 minutes and roared from behind to beat UCF. Weigman's third rushing touchdown, a 1-yard plunge with 10:15 to play, gave Houston (4-1, 1-1 Big 12) its first lead. On the ensuing drive, Weigman -- who finished with 239 passing yards -- connected with Trent Walker for a 43-yard catch-and-run to set the table for Jonathan Dimas' 40-yard field goal with 4:14 to play. Keyone Jenkins passed for 253 yards and a touchdown and ran for another score to lead UCF's (3-2, 1-1) attack. Josh Derry caught seven passes for 101 yards and one touchdown. No. 21 SMU 25, Boston College 16 The host Mustangs carried a three-point lead into halftime and nearly pitched a second-half shutout in a win over the Eagles. Kevin Jennings threw touchdowns to Randy Pittman Jr. and Derrick McFall after intermission, finishing 20-for-30 passing for 160 yards. SMU (4-1, 2-1 ACC) sacked Boston College quarterback Mason McKenzie five times and held the Eagles (2-3, 0-2) scoreless over seven straight possessions from the first quarter until a touchdown with 2:07 left in regulation. Marques White recorded three of the five sacks. McKenzie also threw for two scores and 208 yards on a 20-of-31 passing day. He also led all ball carriers with 74 yards on 21 attempts. Evan Dickens and Danny Edgehill each caught one touchdown pass. No. 22 Boise State 37, Utah State 18 Maddux Madsen passed for two touchdowns and Dylan Riley rushed for two scores as the Broncos ran away with a victory over the Aggies in the inaugural Pac-12 contest for both teams at Boise, Idaho. Madsen completed 17 of 21 passes for 244 yards as the Broncos (4-1, 1-0 Pac-12) defeated Utah State for the 11th consecutive time and 23rd time in the past 24 meetings. Matt Wagner and Ben Ford caught touchdown passes for Boise State, which also saw Jake Ripp return an interception for a touchdown. Javen Jacobs caught a touchdown pass and rushed for 139 yards on 10 carries, including gains of 64 and 46 yards for Utah State (1-4, 0-1). Eli Wood had seven receptions for 102 yards and a touchdown. Grady Brosterhous completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards and two touchdowns. No. 24 Kentucky 35, South Carolina 34 (OT) Kenny Minchey's two-point-conversion pass to Willie Rodriguez lifted the Wildcats to an overtime win over the Gamecocks in Columbia, S.C. Minchey connected with Henry Boyer on a 6-yard touchdown to set up the successful two-point attempt and cap the largest road comeback in program history after Kentucky (4-1, 2-1 SEC) trailed 17-0 in the second quarter. Minchey had 272 passing yards and three touchdowns. LaNorris Sellers threw for 226 yards and two touchdowns while rushing 17 times for 147 yards. Matt Fuller and Jabree Coleman each had a rushing touchdown, while Mazeo Bennett Jr. had 92 receiving yards, and DJ Black and Brown each caught a touchdown pass for South Carolina (2-3, 0-3). --Field Level Media

item.title: Tarik Skubal pitches Dodgers past Braves in Game 1 of NLDS
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Tarik Skubal dominated over six innings, three home runs powered the offense and the Los Angeles Dodgers opened the National League Division Series with a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- Tarik Skubal dominated over six innings, three home runs powered the offense and the Los Angeles Dodgers opened the National League Division Series with a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Saturday. Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Max Muncy all went deep as the Dodgers started their quest to become the first National League club to win three consecutive championships and the first major league team to do it since the New York Yankees from 1998-2000. Skubal (1-0) gave up one run on two hits with two walks and seven strikeouts in his first postseason start for Los Angeles after arriving in a trade-deadline deal from the Detroit Tigers. Sean Murphy and Ozzie Albies hit home runs for the Braves, who entered off a wild-card round victory over the Philadelphia Phillies and are trying to advance past the NLDS for the first time since winning the World Series in 2021. Left-hander Dylan Dodd opened the game with three scoreless innings for Atlanta before giving way to Victor Mederos (0-1), who gave up Hernandez's home run and recorded just one out in the fourth inning. On a blisteringly hot day, with the temperature at 100 degrees to open the game, Skubal allowed only one hit through his first five scoreless innings on the mound. Hernandez backed Skubal with a two-run home run in the fourth inning for a 2-0 advantage. "I really don't care if I strike out in big situations. I always want to be the guy to be in those moments," Hernandez said. "I worked really hard for it, and I think the bigger the moment, the more focused I get. Just trying to put together a good at-bat for the team. Obviously if I get a good pitch to hit, I just try to put a good swing on it." The Braves finally got to Skubal in the sixth when Murphy hit a home run to center to bring Atlanta to within a run. The Dodgers increased their advantage in the bottom of the sixth against AJ Smith-Shawver when Tucker slugged a two-run home run and Muncy followed two batters later with a solo shot down the line in right field for a 5-1 advantage. Tucker's contribution on offense came after a disappointing regular season when his .715 OPS was lower than all but one Dodgers player who played in at least 90 games. Tucker is in the first season of a four-year, $240 million contract. Albies got the Braves within two runs in the ninth with a two-run home run off Tanner Scott. Evan Phillips entered the game with two outs and walked Mauricio Dubon to bring the tying run to the plate. But he earned the save by retiring Austin Riley on a groundout to short. "I thought we put up some competitive at-bats. Really nice swing from Murphy right there and then and then not giving up," Riley said. "With Ozzie, the two-run homer, that was encouraging. Just ran out of time today." --Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.title: Trump names intelligence chief Clayton as AI czar, to head task force
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton the administration's AI czar, tasking him with coordinating the federal government's efforts to maintain US leadership in the technology.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had named Director of National Intelligence [USN:L1N4400P3 TEXT:"Jay Clayton"] the administration's AI czar, tasking him with coordinating the federal government's efforts to maintain US leadership in the technology. Trump, who has pushed to rename artificial intelligence as "super intelligence," said Clayton would head the newly created Super Intelligence Force (SIF), overseeing the government's engagement with consumers, religious groups, AI companies and other stakeholders. In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump wrote that SIF would aim to "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence" and to "protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans." The announcement confirmed a Wall Street Journal report in which Clayton, appointed intelligence chief in August, said Trump had tapped him to lead the administration's push to keep the US at the forefront of AI. "The risk of not being first is high," Clayton told the newspaper. Clayton said the task force would have 120 days to produce a report assessing the risks and opportunities posed by AI and recommending what role the federal government should play. The safety of AI has become a major issue in recent weeks, with some researchers warning that people building the technology believe it could [USN:L4N45616J TEXT:"kill humans within a decade."] Several Democratic and Republican lawmakers have responded with alarm and calls for more action. Trump has appeared to take a [USN:FWN45G0T8 TEXT:"light touch"] toward AI regulation, arguing that excessive oversight could weaken competitiveness against China. He said on Tuesday that he [USN:RTV7Cd7Qt TEXT:"does not want to work"] with Chinese President Xi Jinping on governing AI technology. Clayton's panel will review AI-related risks and current government reporting mechanisms for breaches, hacks and other incidents, and recommend ways to strengthen federal-response capabilities under existing authorities, the Journal said, citing the task force's charter. This is the second time Trump has named an adviser to oversee AI-related decisions across the administration. Venture capitalist David Sacks held the AI czar role at the beginning of Trump's second term. In addition to Clayton, the task force's leaders will include Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor, Trump wrote. The panel will report to the president and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, he said.

item.title: 北朝鮮、3日に中距離ミサイル発射 極超音速兵器の部隊訓練と国営通信
item.description: [ソウル ４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ソウル ４日 ロイター] - 北朝鮮は４日、金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記の立ち会いの下で３日に極超音速ミサイルの発射実験を行ったと発表した。核抑止力の信頼性を示すことを目的とした訓練だとした。国営朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）が伝えた。

ミサイル発射については、金総書記の妹で朝鮮労働党の金与正総務部長が３日に公表していた。ＫＣＮＡが４日に発射に関する詳細を明らかにした。

ＫＣＮＡによると、ミサイルは極超音速戦略兵器システムの一部をなす中距離戦略ミサイルで、東部から発射され、約１０００キロ離れた日本海上の目標に命中した。ミサイル部隊を訓練するとともに、抑止戦力の効率性と機動性を評価するのが目的とした。

金総書記は、こうした活動は抑止力行使の一形態だとし、戦略攻撃兵器の「信頼性と致命性」を敵に認識させる努力を続けなければならないと述べた。核戦争抑止力の開発は国家の安全保障に不不可欠で、この方針に変わりはないと改めて表明したという。

日韓の防衛当局は３日、北朝鮮が弾道ミサイルを発射したと発表した。韓国はミサイルの飛行距離を７００キロ程度、日本は６８０キロ程度と分析している。

＜日韓のミサイル追跡能力に言及＞

金与正氏は３日、韓国と日本がミサイルを追跡できなかったと主張。変則的に飛行する「波状軌道」を採用したことで、両国の追跡能力の限界が露呈したとした。

これに対し、韓国国防省は４日、発射の準備を韓国軍が綿密に監視していたとし、発射直後にミサイルを探知・追跡し、発射地点も正確に特定したと説明した。その上で、北朝鮮が最近発射したミサイルは、韓国と米国のミサイル防衛資産で探知・迎撃できる能力の範囲内にあると評価しているとした。

ＫＣＮＡは今回、正確な着弾座標を含め、異例なほど詳しい情報を公開した。

韓国統一研究院のホン・ミン上級研究員は、こうした情報公開は、ミサイルが約１０００キロ飛行したとの主張を裏付けるとともに、北朝鮮が指摘する、韓国と日本の追跡能力の弱点を浮き彫りにすることが狙いとみている。

ホン氏によると、ミサイルは２０２２年に初めて発射実験が行われた円錐形の極超音速システムとみられる。北朝鮮が実験段階から実戦配備への移行を示唆している可能性があるという。

北朝鮮が弾道ミサイルを発射したのは９月２０日以来。今回は、非武装地帯（ＤＭＺ）で発生した地雷の爆発を巡って韓国と非難の応酬を続ける中で実施した。

韓国は、北朝鮮の地雷で自国の兵士が重傷を負ったと主張。与正氏は２日、韓国側の非難を「根拠がない」として一蹴し、韓国側の謝罪要求も退けている。

item.title: ウクライナ、ロシア製油所攻撃を強化へ 「新ドクトリンに対抗」
item.description:
Daniel Flynn Olena Harmash
［キーウ ３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Daniel Flynn　Olena Harmash

［キーウ　３日　ロイター］ - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、ロシアがキーウなどの都市から住民を退去させることを狙った新たな空爆方針を打ち出したとして、対抗措置としてロシアの製油所への攻撃を強化すると述べた。ただ、民間人は標的にしないと強調した。ロイターのインタビューで語った。

ゼレンスキー氏によると、ウクライナの情報機関は、ロシアのプーチン大統領が冬を前に、これまでよりはるかに広範な民間施設への軍事攻撃を認める「新たなドクトリン」を示した文書を入手した。

ゼレンスキー氏は「われわれは文書を確認しており、インフラや物流施設、特に都市や村、あらゆる場所の道路、学校、病院への攻撃を認めていることを把握している」と説明。「首都や各地の都市から立ち去るよう住民に圧力をかける。これが作戦の目的だ」と述べた。

背景には、前線の重要地域でロシア軍が支配地を失い、死傷者も増える中、プーチン氏が強さを誇示したいと考えていることがあると指摘した。

ロシア大統領府のコメントは得られていない。一方、ロシア外務省は、外国人にキーウからの退去を促す声明で、ここ数カ月のウクライナによる対ロシア攻撃への報復として、今後も組織的な攻撃を続けると表明した。

item.title: North Korea says Kim oversaw hypersonic missile drill
item.description: North Korea said on Sunday it had tested a hypersonic missile under the supervision of leader Kim Jong Un, in a drill aimed at demonstrating the reliability of its nuclear deterrent.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea said on Sunday it had tested a hypersonic missile under the supervision of leader Kim Jong Un, in a drill aimed at demonstrating the reliability of its nuclear deterrent. State media KCNA said the intermediate-range strategic missile, which it described as part of a hypersonic strategic weapon system, was launched on Saturday from eastern North Korea and struck a target about 1,000 km (621 miles) away in waters off the country's east coast. The drill was aimed at training missile troops and assessing the efficiency and mobility of North Korea's deterrent forces, the report said. KCNA quoted Kim as saying North Korea must continue efforts to make its adversaries recognise the "reliability and fatality" of its strategic offensive weapons, calling such activities a form of deterrence. He also reaffirmed that developing the country's nuclear war deterrent remained indispensable for national security and that there would be no change in that policy, KCNA said. The launch was the latest in a series of North Korean weapons tests this year and came as tensions on the Korean peninsula escalated over a landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone last month that wounded South Korean soldiers. TRACKING DISPUTE The KCNA report provided additional details about the missile launch [USN:L1N45P02K TEXT:"disclosed"] on Saturday by Kim Yo Jong, the sister of Kim Jong Un and a senior official in the ruling Workers' Party. Kim Yo Jong said South Korea and Japan had failed to track the weapon's flight, saying a special "wave-like trajectory mode" had exposed limitations in their tracking capabilities. However, South Korea's Defence Ministry said on Sunday that its military had closely monitored preparations for the launch, detected and tracked the missile immediately after liftoff and accurately identified the launch site. The ministry also said North Korea's recently launched missiles were assessed to be within the capabilities of South Korean and US missile-defence assets to detect and intercept. South Korea's military said on Saturday it had assessed the missile flew more than 700 km toward the sea off its eastern coast. KCNA released unusually detailed information about the test, including precise impact coordinates. Hong Min, a senior researcher at the Korea Institute for National Unification, said the disclosure appeared aimed at supporting North Korea's claim that the missile flew about 1,000 km and highlighting what Pyongyang sees as shortcomings in South Korean and Japanese tracking. The missile appeared to be a cone-shaped hypersonic system first tested in 2022, he said, suggesting North Korea was signalling a shift from testing toward operational deployment. Kim Yo Jong on Friday issued a sharply worded statement [USN:L1N45O07Z TEXT:"rejecting"] Seoul's demand for an apology over the DMZ landmine blast, saying its claims were "groundless" and that North Korea had not deliberately laid mines targeting South Korean troops. North Korea has carried out more than 10 missile tests this year.

item.title: フーシ派、リヤドのアラムコ施設攻撃と発表 サウジの攻撃に報復
item.description: ［３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３日　ロイター］ - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は３日、サウジアラビアの首都リヤドにあるサウジアラムコの施設を弾道ミサイルと無人機で攻撃したと発表した。イエメンの首都サヌアやその他の州へのサウジの攻撃に対する報復だとしている。

これに先立ち、リヤドにあるアラムコ施設の近くから大量の煙と炎が上がったとの目撃者情報が出ていた。

アラムコ施設への攻撃について、サウジ当局は今のところ確認していない。アラムコもコメント要請に応じていない。

サウジとフーシ派の衝突は激しさを増し、フーシ派はサウジの都市やエネルギーインフラへの攻撃を強めている。

フーシ派は先週、サウジ西部ヤンブーにあるアラムコの施設をミサイルと無人機で攻撃したと発表した。サウジはその際、フーシ派がタイフとヤンブー周辺に向けて撃った弾道ミサイル６発を撃墜したと説明したが、アラムコ施設の被害については明らかにしなかった。

item.title: White Sox gain ALDS edge with Munetaka Murakami HR, shutout pitching
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Munetaka Murakami belted a two-run homer off All-Star Parker Messick and five pitchers combined on a three-hitter as the Chicago White Sox beat the Cleveland Guardians 3-0 in Game 1 of the American League Division Series on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Munetaka Murakami belted a two-run homer off All-Star Parker Messick and five pitchers combined on a three-hitter as the Chicago White Sox beat the Cleveland Guardians 3-0 in Game 1 of the American League Division Series on Saturday afternoon. Murakami, a 26-year-old rookie from Japan, hammered a 440-foot shot to right field off Messick in the fourth inning. His first postseason homer -- and 36th overall this year -- plated Miguel Vargas to put the White Sox up 2-0. "I was ready, this was the moment I was preparing for the entire season," said Murakami, who yelled toward the visiting dugout as his homer cleared the fence. "I can't explain what I said in words (to the team), but it was a little bit dirty." Chicago extended its lead to 3-0 in the seventh when Colson Montgomery doubled just inside third base against Erik Sabrowski, bringing home Kyle Teel. The White Sox have won three consecutive games to begin their postseason. Bryan Hudson retired the only batter he faced in the third inning for the victory, and closer Grant Taylor tossed the final four innings for the save. Taylor struck out six and allowed a pair of hits. Game 2 of the best-of-five series is Monday afternoon in Cleveland. The White Sox have won eight of the 14 contests between the teams this season, splitting eight games at Progressive Field, the home of the AL Central champion Guardians. "The first game in the series is very important. Now, we'll get the one day (of) rest and focus on winning again," Murakami said. "I can't speak English too much, so the one thing I know is 'Let's go,' and that's it," he added. Messick, a rookie making his postseason debut, struck out six over 4 1/3 innings and allowed two runs on four hits and two walks. The left-hander threw 87 pitches before being replaced by Daniel Espino. Cleveland was held hitless until the fourth, when Travis Bazzana doubled with two outs against Anthony Kay. The Guardians would load the bases with two out for the second straight inning, but Brayan Rocchio lined out to right. "Of course, you're frustrated when you get shut out," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "We just couldn't get it going early in the inning to get some action going. But we didn't get down." White Sox rookie Hagen Smith worked as an opener for the second time this week, tossing 2 2/3 scoreless innings. The left-hander did not give up a hit, struck out four and walked three. Smith retired the first eight Cleveland batters before walking Rocchio, Steven Kwan and Jose Ramirez in the third, prompting White Sox manager Will Venable to lift him for Hudson. The 6-foot-8 left-hander retired lefty-swinging Chase DeLauter on a fly to left to end the inning. Jordan Hicks followed Hudson and recorded two outs before Kay entered. The Guardians' Jo Adell struck out four times in four plate appearances in the first playoff game of his seven-year career. He was acquired from the Los Angeles Angels at the trade deadline. "I was definitely in a blender today, getting different looks every time up from a different pitcher," Adell said. "We've got to adjust because we were trying to find it all day. Postseason is a pitcher's duel and we've got to bounce back." Chicago catcher Teel was unsuccessful on his first ABS challenge after going 5-for-5 in the wild-card round. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

Oct 3 : A former OpenAI safety employee who recently resigned criticized the company's approach to AI safety, arguing that a fast-paced culture focused on rapid development increases the risk of failures. Writing in "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken," published by the Atlantic on Saturday, David Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and should place greater emphasis on safety expertise and research before developing more capable systems. • "The time for trial and error is over," Robinson wrote, arguing that advanced AI systems require safeguards more akin to those used in industries such as nuclear power and aviation. • Robinson said OpenAI relies heavily on what it calls "iterative deployment," releasing systems and strengthening safeguards when problems emerge.

• The comments add to a debate within the AI industry over whether companies are moving too quickly to develop increasingly powerful systems. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have faced scrutiny after incidents in which safety controls failed, or experimental systems behaved unexpectedly. • Robinson, who said he spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches, wrote: "As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed." • "We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement. • Robinson also warned that AI capabilities were advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems act in accordance with human goals and values.

item.title: Trump shares Republican senator's phone number in feud over time switch
item.description: Less afternoon sunlight makes it harder to play more than 14 holes of golf, Trump said.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump shared online the supposed phone number of a Republican US senator on Saturday in an escalating dispute over making daylight saving time permanent. In a social media post, the president urged people to call a phone number he said belonged to Senator Tom Cotton, an Arkansas Republican who opposes the Trump-backed Sunshine Protection Act. The act would end the twice-yearly practice of changing clocks by one hour. Trump says most Americans want more afternoon sunlight, but Cotton has argued the change would plunge early risers into darkness in winter. "Everybody in Arkansas, Tom Cotton, a friend of mine, is holding up a very important Bill," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. Cotton did not directly respond to Trump's statement, but posted on X: "No one likes changing the clock, me included, but Congress has enacted permanent Daylight Savings Time multiple times before and repealed it each time once Americans experienced absurdly late sunrises in the winter. "Arkansans don't want their kids going to school in the pitch dark, and I'll always put Arkansas first." When Reuters called the number Trump gave for Cotton, it went directly to a voicemail box that did not identify itself as belonging to the senator. Supporters of permanent daylight saving time say adjusting clocks disrupts sleep and increases road accidents, while critics argue later winter sunrises would leave children traveling to school and commuters heading to work in the dark. GOLFING ARGUMENT Trump on Saturday published three Truth Social posts — one in the morning and two in the afternoon — focused on daylight saving time. In a subsequent five-minute session with journalists at the White House, he spent more than half the time talking about the twice-yearly practice of changing clocks by one hour . Most US states have observed the time switch since the 1960s. Clocks this year are slated to switch back to standard time on November 1. "It discombobulates everybody," Trump said, complaining to reporters that losing afternoon daylight caused lateness for meetings and dinner and made it difficult to play more than 14 holes of golf. He also suggested that more daylight would reduce crime. "You know who wants it? The farmers want it. You know who wants it? Sports want it," Trump told reporters before heading to a [USN:L1N45O0PX TEXT:"campaign rally in Ohio"] . "Professional sports and amateurs that would like to play tennis at night, would like to play golf a little bit without having to run home after 14 holes." Trump, an avid golfer, earlier shared an October 1 letter from PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp, writing: "The PGA TOUR, as an example, needs more Daylight in the afternoon in order to finish their Tournaments." POLITICAL CONSIDERATIONS After Cotton published his statement, the president responded with a post that framed the matter in political terms. "Give the Republican Party a Senatorial WIN, for a change! … TAKE THE WIN TOM, JUST TAKE THE WIN! YOU NEED IT, AND SO DOES OUR BELOVED REPUBLICAN PARTY!" Trump wrote. Cotton is running for reelection but his race is not considered competitive, as Trump received more than 64% of the Arkansas vote in the 2024 presidential election. The US House of Representatives passed the bill in July, but Cotton is not alone in the Senate. Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, this week called the bill "[USN:L1N45O0H3 TEXT:"dead as disco"]" and said he did not think that Senate Majority Leader John Thune would bring the measure for a vote. The offices of Cotton and Thune did not respond to requests for comment. Saturday's post targeting Cotton is not the first time Trump has shared a senator's phone number to make a point. During his first presidential campaign in 2015, Trump [USN:KCN0PV26U TEXT:"read"] Senator Lindsey Graham's phone number at a rally and dismissed the South Carolina Republican as an "idiot." They later reconciled, with the [USN:L6N43E02O TEXT:"late Graham"] becoming one of Trump's highest-profile allies in Congress.

item.title: Ukraine will hit Russian refineries in response to Moscow's 'new doctrine' of airstrikes, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Vladimir Putin called for broader attacks on civilian targets, Volodymyr Zelenskiy told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukraine will double down on attacking Russian oil refineries in response to a new policy of airstrikes by Moscow designed to [USN:L8N44V1KC TEXT:"force people to abandon Kyiv"] and other cities, but will not target civilians, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Ukraine's intelligence services has obtained documents showing that Russian leader Vladimir Putin had issued a "new doctrine" of military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter, Zelenskiy said. "We saw documents and we know that they allow them to attack infrastructure, logistics, and especially to attack in the cities, in the villages, everywhere, roads, schools, hospitals," Zelenskiy told Reuters in an interview. "To pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities: this is the goal of the operation." Driving the shift in policy, Zelenskiy said, was Putin's desire to appear strong at a time when his military was losing ground in a key frontline region and sustaining higher levels of casualties. The Kremlin was not available to comment on Saturday. But in a statement [USN:L1N45P03K TEXT:"urging foreign nationals to leave Kyiv"], the Russian Foreign Ministry said Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia in recent months. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians. COUNTEROFFENSIVE IN DONBAS Zelenskiy said a successful Ukrainian counteroffensive, code-named "Vivaldi", had recaptured around 140 sq km (54 sq miles) of Ukrain's eastern Donbas region and was still ongoing. Russia has said it must control Donbas in its entirety as a condition for any peace deal. In recent weeks, US President Donald Trump's administration has sought to revive talks to end the four-year-old conflict – Europe's bloodiest since World War Two. The US leader last month urged Ukraine [USN:L1N45503J TEXT:"to refrain from hitting Russian oil installations"], saying that was sending global diesel prices surging. But Zelenskiy, speaking as air raid sirens blared outside the gilded halls of the presidential offices, said he had received no indications from Russia that Putin was interested in peace talks, or discussing a ceasefire on energy infrastructure. Over the past week, the Ukrainian capital has come under persistent attack by Russian drones and missiles targeting energy and telecoms assets, road and rail infrastructure. For the first time, Russia has [USN:L1N45P00Z TEXT:"targeted the bridges"] across the Dnipro river connecting east and west Kyiv. Zelenskiy said Ukraine would react to the change in tactics by Moscow, but would not target civilian infrastructure indiscriminately. "We have to respond in any way (we can). With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners etc: what gives money to them for this war," Zelenskiy said in English. "But we will not respond, of course, just like them, on any civilian objects." SUPPORT FROM EUROPE After the Trump administration invited Putin [USN:L6N45F16H TEXT:"to attend a G20 summit in Miami"] in December and discussed business deals with Russian envoys, Zelenskiy urged Washington not to normalise relations with Russia before ensuring a return to peace. Zelenskiy said he would be happy to meet Putin for peace talks at the G20, but he warned the US not to believe in "illusions" that Russia would simply end hostilities if it gained control of Donbas. "It's not fair just to normalise," said Zelenskiy, dressed in his trademark black T-shirt and military-style jacket. Any resumption of economic and diplomatic ties with the West had to be in return for Russia ending hostilities, he said: "Because peace is more important than any kind of economy." While the US has proposed a resumption of trilateral talks in the coming weeks in the UAE, Zelenskiy noted that an exact date and location for the technical-level conversations had still not been set. Ukrainian officials warn that Russia has stockpiled hundreds of ballistic missiles ahead of an expected winter onslaught against electricity and water infrastructure. Last winter, the worst of the war, Russian strikes left swathes of the country without electricity and heating for days at a time. Since the summer, Moscow has also begun launching dozens of fast and relatively cheap jet-powered Shahed drones a day at Ukraine, whose air defence teams have struggled to cope because their interceptor drones were too slow to catch them. Zelenskiy said Ukraine had been forced to rely heavily on its fighter aircraft – F-16s and MiGs – to down around 60% of the Russian jet-powered drones, but supplies of 20 mm ammunition for the planes were running low. Kyiv was urgently working on other solutions – including boosting its electronic jamming capabilities, he said. In the second half of October, it would receive the first shipment of small, cheap air defence missiles capable of hitting the new Shaheds. Last week, Zelenskiy said Ukraine was developing five models of new interceptor drones capable of downing the jet Shaheds. Fresh from a meeting with his defence chiefs, he said tests on two of those models showed a modest success rate of around 30%. "We'll have to scale it," he said. "I hope that with all these things, with all these elements, we'll find a way." BALLISTIC THREAT Ukraine announced the first combat use this week of its own domestically made ballistic missile, the FP-7, which has a range of around 250 km (155 miles). Zelenskiy said he had called the manufacturer Fire Point to pressure executives to finish a longer-range model, the FP-9, which the company has said could hit Moscow. "I said to them, where is my FP-9?" said Zelenskiy, with a grin. "We need the FP-9. And the FP-9 will be (ready) this autumn, I'm sure." Zelenskiy said a recent spate of Russian drone incursions and hybrid attacks in Europe were an effort to intimidate European populations and to undermine support for Ukraine. Some European leaders were starting to understand this, he said, and toughen their position. Russia says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria. After talks with European officials in Brussels this week, Ukraine had unlocked funding to order the drones that it needs to keep fighting at the start of 2027, Zelenskiy said. Ukrainian officials had worked on plans with European partners to plug a $27 billion hole in Kyiv's defence budget this year. The plans involve a combination of the reallocation of Ukraine's own budget resources, bilateral assistance and using "money credits" from next year's portion of a €90 billion EU loan, Zelenskiy said. "We will close this (gap). I think this is absolutely a big success for our country," he said.

item.title: Lula ahead in polls for Brazil's first-round vote; runoff likely
item.description: A series of polls on Saturday showed Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva slightly ahead of Senator Flavio Bolsonaro before Sunday's first-round vote, and a close race in a likely runoff between the leftist incumbent and his right-wing challenger.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A series of polls on Saturday showed Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva slightly ahead of Senator Flavio Bolsonaro before Sunday's first-round vote, and a close race in a likely runoff between the leftist incumbent and his right-wing challenger. If no candidate wins more than 50% of valid votes -- which exclude blank and null ballots -- on Sunday, the two frontrunners advance to a second-round runoff on October 25. item.title: US Coast Guard finds debris from missing medical aircraft off Nantucket
item.description: The US Coast Guard said late on Saturday it found debris from a medical transport aircraft off the shore of Massachusetts' Nantucket island and was searching for six people who were on board.
item.dc:creator: Sheila Dang, Lisa Richwine
item.content:encoded: The US Coast Guard said late on Saturday it found debris from a medical transport aircraft off the shore of Massachusetts' Nantucket island and was searching for six people who were on board. The Federal Aviation Administration told the Coast Guard early on Saturday that it had lost contact with a Gulfstream jet traveling from Bermuda to Boston. Several hours later, the Coast Guard said in a statement that it "located a debris field that has been confirmed to be associated with the missing aircraft." Four Canadians were on the plane, Canadian Minister of Transport Steven MacKinnon said on X. "We are closely monitoring the situation and are working with the relevant authorities as search and rescue efforts continue," he wrote. The other two passengers were Bermudian nationals, the Coast Guard said. Searches will continue throughout the night near Nantucket, an island community south of mainland Massachusetts, they said. The aircraft, registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, departed Bermuda at 12:41 a.m. on Saturday (0301 GMT), according to data from flight tracking website FlightAware. The plane was flying at 24,000 feet (7,300 metres) for much of the flight before descending 13,000 feet in about two minutes shortly before flight controllers lost contact, data showed. Local TV station Boston 25 posted an audio clip from Boston Logan International Airport in which an air traffic controller can be heard asking the Gulfstream pilot, "You said you're coming in blind? Is that what you said?" The controller then asked whether the plane was declaring an emergency. No response was heard. Latitude is based in Ontario, Canada, and provides medical evacuation services. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Bermuda government is in contact with US authorities and the families of the passengers, Bermuda Premier David Burt wrote in a statement posted on Instagram. "We are praying that all six people will be found safe," he wrote.

LONDON: Two Iranian nationals appeared in a London court on Saturday (Oct 3) charged with plotting acts of terrorism involving the use of a homemade bomb to attack the Jewish community in northern England at the behest of a figure believed to be based in Iran. Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were arrested on Sep 20 at the start of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, when they are accused of carrying out "hostile" surveillance on potential Jewish targets in Manchester, prosecutors say. These targets included the Manchester Jewish Museum and Heaton Park synagogue, the scene of a deadly attack almost a year ago in which two Jewish worshippers were killed, prosecutor Mark Luckett told Westminster Magistrates' Court. ALLEGED PLOT INVOLVED HOMEMADE DEVICE "Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device," Luckett said.

He said the men were accused of being in contact with a third party who is alleged to have directed and coordinated the attack planning and provided instructions on how to assemble a homemade device, which prosecutors allege would have been made from chlorine and brake fluid. "It's assessed that this individual is also an Iranian national and most likely operating from within Iran," Luckett said.

Related:

UK's Starmer convenes community leaders to fight antisemitism after attacks

Two Jewish men stabbed in London, police treat attack as terrorism

The court was told both men had come to Britain from Europe in small boats. Salehi had arrived in 2020 and had been granted asylum, while Ahmadyan came in 2023 and his asylum claim was still outstanding, Luckett said. The men did not enter a plea and were remanded in custody until their next hearing at London's Old Bailey court on Oct 23. The case comes a week after Britain said Iran was believed to be involved in a suspected plot to target the RAF Fairford air base which the US military has used to carry out raids against targets in Iran, leading to a dual British-Iranian national being arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. Police said on Saturday he had been released on police bail while the investigation continues. British counterterrorism police have said the Manchester allegations were not connected in any way to the Fairford investigation. Iran has rejected accusations of involvement in a number of plots in Britain in recent years, and said allegations it was connected to the Fairford incident were baseless. Britain has also seen a significant rise in antisemitism since the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023 that triggered the subsequent war in Gaza, including a series of attacks on Jewish sites in London earlier this year. "It is no secret that this country faces a range of serious threats from the Iranian regime," Home Secretary (interior minister) Shabana Mahmood said in a statement. "They target our Jewish communities and try to silence their critics overseas, often through proxies and criminal networks to hide their involvement."

Source: Reuters/ec

item.title: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Aramco facility in Riyadh with missiles, drones
item.description: Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Saturday they had targeted an Aramco facility in the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, saying the attack was in retaliation for Saudi attacks on Yemen's Sanaa and other provinces. A large plume of smoke and fire was seen rising in the vicinity of an Aramco facility in Riyadh earlier on Saturday, a witness told Reuters. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities of an attack on an Aramco facility. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The reported attack comes amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure. The Houthis said last week they had attacked Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu with missiles and drones. Saudi Arabia said at the time that it had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards Taif and the Yanbu area, but did not report damage to Aramco facilities.

item.title: In crude Ohio rally speech, Trump says he may not help if Democrats win
item.description: "Just get out and vote," Trump said at a rally for Republican candidates. "If you do that, we're going to win, and we're going to win big, and we're going to shove it up their ass."
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Nandita Bose
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump used an Ohio rally on Saturday to mix profane attacks on Democrats with promises of financial help if Republicans win the midterms and a warning that he would be less willing to work with the state if Democrats prevail. "Just get out and vote," Trump said at a rally for Republican candidates, including US Senator Jon Husted and Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. "If you do that, we're going to win, and we're going to win big, and we're going to shove it up their ass." Multiple incumbent Republican senators across the country face tough political headwinds in the November 3 elections, with Trump's [USN:L6N45D0XN TEXT:"popularity falling"] in recent months as higher prices persist for gasoline and other staples amid the US-Israeli war with Iran. Both Husted and Ramaswamy are in competitive races against Democratic opponents. Former US Senator Sherrod Brown is running against Husted. Amy Acton is facing Ramaswamy. OHIO A KEY STATE IN MIDTERMS Polls have suggested that Democrats could gain ground in the midterms, which will decide control of the narrowly divided House of Representatives and Senate, but Trump said Republicans would do better than critics expect. "I think we're going to have a big surprise because they don't know what's happening," he told the crowd in Vandalia, Ohio. Ohio's is among eight US Senate races rated competitive. The state has turned into a campaign battlefield over [USN:L6N45916H TEXT:"data centers"] and culture war issues such as youth transgender surgeries. Trump repeatedly attacked Democrats during his speech, at one point calling them "dumb son of a bitches," while arguing that maintaining Republican control would give Ohio officials a direct line to his administration and make it easier for the state to secure federal help. He said Ohio's elected Republican officials frequently call him seeking money for the state, adding that he would be less inclined to accommodate Democrats if they win key races. Referring to Acton, Trump said: "But I'm not going to help her." Husted is counting on Trump to motivate supporters who might otherwise skip the midterms, but the senator also directly criticized Brown, a veteran Democrat, as someone who has accomplished little in his political career. "He's been in office for 50 years — can you name one thing that he has done for you?" Husted said at the rally. A spokesperson for Brown's campaign criticized Husted for backing Trump's policy on Iran and said Husted supported "sweetheart tax deals" that lured data centers to Ohio. "Jon Husted puts corporations and billionaires first every time, and we all pay for it," Brown spokesperson Lauren Chou said in an email to Reuters. Trump garnered more than 55% of the Ohio vote in the 2024 presidential election, but economic concerns since then have sunk his approval ratings. Ohio gasoline prices increased 35% over the past year to $4.16 per gallon on average, according to AAA, which compiles data on automobile travel. Trump's trade policy with Canada has led to retaliatory Canadian tariffs that affect about $3 billion worth of Ohio exports, based on 2025 figures, according to a CBC report. DEBATE ON DATA CENTERS Talking to reporters shortly before addressing Saturday's rally, Husted said the US has to win the Iran war "on our terms" and in the interim, he is "showing people that I'm fighting for lower prices." He spoke to a sympathetic crowd at the rally, but he also needs to sell his message to people like independent voter Jonathan Smith. Smith, a 19-year-old construction worker, held a sign reading, "Where are my lower gas prices?" outside his former high school in Vandalia, north of Dayton. "I've got a wedding to save up for, and with gas prices continuously going up, it's getting harder and harder to put aside money," said Smith, adding he is still deciding whom to vote for in the Senate race. Outside political groups have poured [USN:L6N458188 TEXT:"tens of millions"] of dollars into Ohio, making Husted-Brown the second-most-expensive Senate race in the country, according to Federal Election Commission filings. Rallygoers shared mixed opinions on the hot-button issue of data centers in the state. "I'm not huge on the AI data centers," Samuel Clevenger, 20, said when discussing Husted's candidacy. But the apprentice plumber said he was encouraged to vote by Trump's attention to the state, as well as his 2025 policy capping taxes on overtime. On the other side of the rally venue, Brenda White, 60, held a sign encouraging building in her northeastern Ohio town: "DATA CENTER SOUTH LORAIN." As Husted met voters in the bleachers, she urged the senator to support the center's construction in place of a steel mill. "You want a data center there?" Husted asked. Before White posed for her photo with Husted, a man in the senator's entourage asked: "Can we do it without the sign?"

item.title: New term gives US Supreme Court's Thomas and Alito more chances to wield power
item.description: The two oldest and most conservative justices are at the height of their influence.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The new US Supreme Court term that begins on Monday presents opportunities for its two eldest and most conservative justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, to help push US law further rightward on contentious issues such as gun rights, religion in public schools and voting restrictions. Thomas, 78, has served on the top US judicial body since 1991, making him the [USN:L1N41E02Q TEXT:"second-longest-serving justice"] in American history. Alito, 76, has served since 2006. Earlier in their tenures, they often found themselves in dissent in major decisions, but the court, with a 6-3 conservative majority since 2020, has shifted dramatically to the right. Thomas and Alito now are perhaps at the height of their influence and have been lavished with praise by Republican President Donald Trump . 'WHY LEAVE?' If either were to retire, that would clear the way for Trump to nominate a younger conservative replacement who could serve for decades in the lifetime position. But, at least for now, according to legal experts, they appear more interested in wielding that power than stepping aside. "They have been waiting for a long time to be in the position," political science professor Kevin McMahon of Trinity College in Connecticut said of Thomas and Alito. "So why leave?" During the court's term that ended in June, Thomas and Alito helped deliver long-sought victories to the conservative legal movement. These included a [USN:S0N3YR013 TEXT:"ruling"] expanding presidential control over regulatory agencies, and a [USN:S0N3YR00L TEXT:"decision"] further limiting the scope of the Voting Rights Act, the landmark 1965 law intended to eliminate racial discrimination in voting. Thomas and Alito have been Trump's most reliable votes in cases involving his extraordinary exertion of presidential powers. [USN:L1N45H0WL TEXT:"More such cases are coming"] during the new nine-month term, including two involving Trump's hardline [USN:S0N43101E TEXT:"immigration policies"]. The court's docket also includes November 3 arguments in a [USN:L1N4130K0 TEXT:"challenge"] to a Colorado law requiring preschools receiving taxpayer money to enroll children of same-sex couples, the latest clash between religious rights and LGBT protections to reach the justices. The justices also may take up a case examining whether a Texas law that requires public elementary and high schools to display the [USN:L1N45G0IM TEXT:"biblical Ten Commandments"] in classrooms comports with the US Constitution's prohibition on the government establishing or endorsing any particular religion or promoting religion over nonreligion. On December 2, the court will [USN:S0N3YR01V TEXT:"hear"] arguments over whether states can ban AR-15s and other semiautomatic rifles, an opportunity for the conservative justices to further expand gun rights. Thomas and Alito have been instrumental in major guns rulings since 2008. On December 8, the court will [USN:S0N41Y01G TEXT:"consider"] whether Arizona can mandate that people registering to vote provide proof of citizenship, a Republican-backed measure critics have called an effort to make it harder for groups who tend to support Democratic candidates to register. Legal experts said these cases give Thomas and Alito chances to build on some of their most influential earlier rulings and target more Supreme Court precedents they consider misguided. "They have more they want to accomplish, and I expect them to keep pushing on a host of issues," McMahon said, adding that they even may envision themselves serving as a check on a potential future Democratic president beginning in 2029. "They're still in their seventies," McMahon said. "And for a Supreme Court justice, it's not unprecedented that you stay on the bench well into your eighties." 'LEGENDS, BOTH' Thomas and Alito backed every major Trump administration policy that came before the court last term, unlike the three conservative justices Trump appointed during his first term — Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett. Those three all have compiled very conservative records as justices but in a few major cases sided against Trump. Trump [USN:L6N45N0QS TEXT:"told"] Time magazine this week he regretted nominating all three, calling them disloyal. "I gave them the position of a lifetime, and they vote against me often," Trump said. Thomas and Alito, on the other hand, are "[USN:FWN4570D3 TEXT:"legends, both"]," Trump said last month after they dissented from a decision that blocked his plans to restrict mail-in voting. "Alito and Thomas are the two who have figured out how to never get into Trump's doghouse," University of Minnesota political science professor Timothy Johnson said. Alito rejected the notion that he is a rubber stamp for Trump and his administration, telling the Wall Street Journal in August: "I vote in every case the way I think the case should be decided. If that means a high correlation with what Trump wants, fine. If it means zero correlation with what Trump wants, fine as well." 'A VALUABLE CONTRIBUTION' Speculation among court watchers about a possible vacancy has ramped up as the two men draw closer to the average age of retirement for Supreme Court justices since 2000 — about 80 years old — and with the November 3 US congressional elections looming. If Democrats take control of the Senate, they could try to block Trump's nominee to fill any vacancy created by the retirement or death of a sitting justice. Alito tamped down retirement speculation for now, telling the Wall Street Journal: "Obviously, I'm here for another term." The term runs through the end of June. In a CBS News interview excerpt released on Friday, Alito said he thought about retiring this year, calling retirement something someone his age must think about every year. "But I thought that I could still make a valuable contribution, which is why I became a justice and a judge in the first place," Alito said. "It's too hard to predict, for anybody, particularly when you reach a certain age, what your situation will be a year from now, two years from now, and so forth," Alito said. "And it's too hard to predict what the political situation will be, and what any president might do with respect to a replacement." ABORTION RIGHTS Alito has a lot of influence in conversations among the court's conservatives, said Peter Canellos, author of a recent Alito biography titled "Revenge for the Sixties." "A lot of the action on the Supreme Court right now is conservative on conservative," Canellos said. "It's entirely a discussion among conservatives." Canellos said Alito's influence was highlighted by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, perhaps the most important ruling he has authored. It overturned the 1973 Roe v. Wade precedent that had recognized a woman's constitutional right to have an abortion. Chief Justice John Roberts, a stalwart conservative, dissented from the portion of Alito's ruling that reversed Roe. "I think over the years Alito has thought of himself as an instrumental justice," Canellos said. "You can see in many cases, Dobbs included, that his key ability is to bring the three Trump appointees to his side, rather than Chief Justice Roberts' side, when the two of them disagree." In Dobbs, Gorsuch, Kavanaugh and Barrett joined Alito. "I suspect that Alito felt that even if he were replaced by a true conservative, which was the core of the argument why he should resign, it was not in any way preordained that that person would have the kind of influence that he has," Canellos added. Alito has long criticized a 1990 Supreme Court precedent that limits the ability of people to seek religious exemptions from generally applicable laws. Religious rights advocates have said that ruling infringes on First Amendment protections for free exercise of religion. The 1990 ruling specifically held that the First Amendment does not protect people who participate in illegal acts — in that case, the use of an illegal hallucinogenic drug — as part of a religious ceremony. The religious freedom case being argued in November, called St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy, gives Alito and the other conservative justices a chance to cast doubt on the 1990 precedent, known as Employment Division v. Smith. 'WHY NOT CONTINUE?' The case involving state-level bans on assault-style rifles may give Thomas a chance to clarify a test he laid out in one of his most impactful rulings, a 2022 case called New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen. Under this test, gun control measures must be "consistent with this nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation" — not simply advance an important government interest — in order to comply with the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms. Some judges have said this wording does not provide clear guidance, producing inconsistent results. "He has clearly expressed frustration that his colleagues have dodged reviews of assault-weapon prohibitions, making these consolidated challenges from Connecticut and Illinois a long-sought vehicle to establish a nationwide constitutional rule that includes these specific guns," Johnson said of Thomas. Thomas has not addressed retirement rumors, but in the past has hinted at a lengthy tenure. McMahon said Thomas may want to become the longest-serving justice, a milestone he would reach in May 2028. "If you're that close, and you have the setup that he has, why not continue?" McMahon asked.

As public fears of AI grow, Trump digs in on voluntary safeguards

WASHINGTON, Oct 3 : US President Donald Trump spent Tuesday showcasing his administration’s approach to AI — touting the US government’s new AI chatbot, dining with tech titans at the White House, and announcing a voluntary agreement with those executives that he said would address growing fears about the technology's safety. The display signaled that Trump is eager to show he is addressing growing voter concerns about AI's dangers without imposing restrictions that could hamper the technology's development, AI safety advocates said. The safety agreement with six companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet’s Google — includes no stated consequences if a company chooses not to comply. Trump described it as “morally binding.” “This was an attempt to give the impression that the government is listening to these concerns without undercutting what has been a very clear and consistent line from this administration: that regulation and governance inherently impede innovation,” said Kat Duffy, who runs an AI team at the nonpartisan Council on Foreign Relations. Whether voters buy Trump's effort in the run-up to US midterm elections on November 3 remains to be seen. Public uneasiness with AI, and the small group of people who seemingly hold sway over it, has risen in recent months. Three-quarters of Americans worry that AI companies have not gone far enough to prevent AI from causing serious harm to society, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published September 22. A series of security events has also underscored how advanced AI can act unpredictably.
